documents.how_used: This is the only official Division document I found that lists the policy content a home care HCSF should have in writing. I used it as the main source for required_items. It is aspirational: where it conflicts with or exceeds N.J.S.A. 34:8-43 et seq. or N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.1 et seq., the statute and rules control. Its fetched text appears to end after the Service Agreement Policy sentence.

documents.how_used: Policies should not conflict with these prohibitions. N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-jersey/N-J-A-C-13-45B-13-3) lists only application paperwork (registration form, criminal-history certifications, bond, other-state licenses). Under the exclusion rules, none of its items were extracted as policy content.

required_items.text: Intake interview and initial assessment: the HCSF, by or through its DON/HCSS, assigns a nurse, office manager or other responsible staff member to conduct an intake interview with the patient and/or family/significant-other.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: For patients discharged from a health care facility, the DON/HCSS or RN on call takes responsibility for delegating care during the first 24 to 48 hours, pending the designated RN's in-person nursing assessment.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: For all other assignments, an RN should conduct an in-person nursing assessment of each patient before care starts, to establish a baseline of physical and functional status and the level of services needed.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: Full name of patient
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 1

required_items.text: Date of birth
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 2

required_items.text: Gender
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 3

required_items.text: Primary Care Provider and/or other health care professional contact information, including name and phone number
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 4

required_items.text: Past medical history, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 5

required_items.text: Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s), if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 6

required_items.text: List of medications, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 7

required_items.text: Functional status, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 8

required_items.text: Family/Significant-Other contact information, including name, phone number and relationship to the patient
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 9

required_items.text: Identification of services in place, additional services needed, and collateral contacts, if applicable
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 10

required_items.text: Name, date and signature of person conducting intake. If history, diagnoses, medications and functional status are not known, the documentation should reflect an attempt to obtain them.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 11

required_items.text: Vital signs, including temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure, and a pain assessment. This assessment is done by the DON/HCSS or an assigned Nurse Supervisor, to determine tasks to delegate to an assigned CHHA, before service starts (or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges).
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 1

required_items.text: Past medical history
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 2

required_items.text: Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s)
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 3

required_items.text: List of medications
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 4

required_items.text: Functional status
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 5

required_items.text: Psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 6

required_items.text: A systems review (neurologic, musculo-skeletal, integumentary, cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, genito-urinary)
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 7

required_items.text: Nutritional status, including diet
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 8

required_items.text: Home safety review, including fall risk assessment
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 9

required_items.text: Emergency plan
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 10

required_items.text: Advance directives
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 11

required_items.text: Primary Care Provider's Certification of Need for Services, if applicable
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 12

required_items.text: Date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor conducting the assessment
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 13

required_items.text: Days and hours of service to be provided to the patient. The Plan of Care is developed by the DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor from the in-person assessment, before service starts (or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges).
Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s)
Tasks to be performed by employees and licensure/registration status of the assigned employees – RNs, LPNs, CHHAs, unlicensed assistive personnel, and therapists
The frequency at which the tasks are to be performed
Short-term and long-term goals for patient care and discharge
Specific changes in patient status that need to be reported to the Nurse Supervisor
Date and signature of the nurse who assessed the patient and developed or modified the Plan of Care
Date and signature of the patient and/or family/significant-other
Date and signature of the employee who is assigned at the start of service

Date and signature of the employee who is assigned at reassessment and whenever there are changes in the Plan of Care. A copy of the Plan of Care is kept in the office and at the patient's residence, and is available to the patient, family/significant others and agency employees.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Plan of Care 10 and following paragraph

required_items.text: Before services start in a new patient's home, assigned CHHAs receive an in-person description and/or demonstration of the delegated tasks from the RN, regardless of experience level. The RN assures the CHHA has the requisite skills and may refuse to delegate to a CHHA who lacks the competencies. A CHHA has a duty to refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently carry out.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Competency Evaluation of Assigned CHHAs Prior to the Start of Services

required_items.text: Date and time of each patient assignment. The CHHA prepares and files a weekly activity sheet with the HCSF.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 1

required_items.text: Documentation of the activities performed, as well as those activities identified in the Plan of Care that were not performed and the reasons why
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 2

required_items.text: Any change in the patient's condition that was reported to the Nursing Supervisor and documented by both the CHHA and nurse
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 3

required_items.text: Date and signature of the CHHA
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 4

required_items.text: Date and signature of patient, family member, significant other or designated party. Records are kept with the patient's medical record in the office for a minimum of 7 years for an adult and 21 years for a pediatric patient, or as required by law.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 5 and retention paragraph

required_items.text: A Nurse Supervisor evaluates care records regularly and contacts the patient and/or significant other at least every 30 days to determine whether the Plan of Care still meets the patient's needs. The clinical record reflects this evaluation.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review and Re-Evaluation

required_items.text: A Nurse Supervisor conducts an in-person re-evaluation every 60 days (or 2 months), or more often if the patient's condition warrants. More frequent re-evaluation also applies after an interruption of service, a hospitalization or facility stay, or a change in condition or functional status, or if consistent with a service agreement.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review and Re-Evaluation

required_items.text: If the nurse changes the plan of care, the documentation reflects the reasons, based on review of: (1) nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s); (2) changes in vital signs, including temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and a pain assessment; (3) changes in functional status; (4) psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care; (5) nutritional status, including diet; (6) home safety review, including fall risk assessment; (7) the emergency plan.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review, list 1-7

required_items.text: The re-evaluation documentation also includes: (1) name of any employees present, their licensure status, and the skill(s) observed; (2) confirmation that the plan of care has been reviewed with the CHHA; (3) any communication with patient, family, significant other or designated party regarding complaints, problems, etc.; (4) date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review, documentation list 1-4

required_items.text: When the Nurse Supervisor directly observes a CHHA's skills, the CHHA's employee file reflects: (1) the skills directly observed; (2) an evaluation of how well those skills were performed; (3) any demonstrations/instructions provided by the Nurse Supervisor, if applicable; (4) the date of the observation; (5) the signature of the employee being evaluated; (6) the signature of the Nurse Supervisor.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Documentation Requirement Relating to the Clinical Performance of the CHHA 1-6

required_items.text: Applicant's name (including any nicknames), address, telephone number and e-mail address, if available. Every applicant for employment involving health care services completes a written application.
Applicant's New Jersey license or certificate number, as applicable, the type of license, the licensing authority and the expiration date of the license
Applicant's date of birth
Applicant's Social Security number

Names, addresses and telephone numbers of all employers during at least the year preceding the application, including (a) names of supervisors, (b) dates of employment, (c) work experience, (d) reasons for leaving each employer

Education and training, including the dates of training, the location where it was obtained, any degrees or certificates received, including attainment of training in CPR, and the dates of issue and expiration, if applicable
Date and signature of applicant
Authorization to conduct a criminal background check
Every applicant for employment is interviewed. The HCSF maintains documentation of the interview, including the name and title of the interviewer and the date of the interview.

Obtain written and/or appropriately documented verbal references from at least two individuals. At least one must be (1) an employer, including an immediate past employer, or (2) an educator, including an instructor from a CHHA training program, if applicable. References do not include family members or friends.

Applicant file documentation includes: (1) name and relationship to the applicant of the person giving the reference; (2) dates of the applicant's employment; (3) content of the reference, including the reasons for leaving employment; (4) for written references, the signature and title of the reference and date signed; (5) for verbal references, the signature of the HCSF staff member who obtained the reference and date of the call. Pre-written letters of recommendation are acceptable if verified by the HCSF.

Before referral or placement of a licensed, certified or registered individual, and after personal examination of the original or other reliable verification source, maintain a copy of every employee's current license, registration or certificate, plus a copy of the Division of Consumer Affairs online verification printout confirming current status.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Verification of Credentials and Content of Personnel Record

required_items.text: Health attestation form, reflecting the results of Mantoux tuberculin skin test as well as rubella and rubeola immunization or serologic evidence of immunity
Clinical competency documentation
Performance evaluations
Clinical supervision documentation
In-service attendance records
Malpractice insurance policy number, if applicable to the individual
Date of hire
Annual verification of licensure status as reflected by the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs' online verification page printout. The agency establishes the yearly date for credentials verification.
A photograph of the employee, with the face clearly visible like those required for a passport, matching the photograph used for the employee's identification badge
Provide an orientation program quarterly to all newly hired CHHAs within three months of employment, or sooner based on the CHHA's documented level of expertise.

Orientation covers at minimum: (1) infection control; (2) blood-borne pathogens; (3) child abuse; (4) elder abuse; (5) domestic violence; (6) pain management; (7) patient rights; (8) HIPAA; (9) corporate compliance; (10) ethical considerations in home care delivery, including receipt of gifts and money from clients and other financial transactions; (11) employee safety; (12) emergency procedures; (13) agency administrative and clinical policies and procedures.

Orientation documentation includes: (1) outline of topics covered; (2) length of time for each of the mandatory in-service topics; (3) date and signature of instructor; (4) name, date and signature of employees on an agency sign-in sheet. Attendance records are maintained and may be electronic if readily retrievable and printable.

Provide an in-service program at least once each year (or over the course of a year) for all CHHAs, covering at minimum: (1) blood-borne pathogens; (2) infection control; (3) standard precautions; (4) child abuse; (5) elder abuse; (6) domestic violence; (7) pain management; (8) workforce protection; (9) employee safety issues; (10) back safety; (11) how to handle needle sticks; (12) fraud and abuse prevention; (13) corporate compliance. An HCSF may accept another HCSF's documentation that a CHHA met some or all of these topics. Attendance records are maintained.

All CHHAs undergo clinical competency testing by a Nurse Supervisor before or on the first date of assignment. This includes direct observation of delegated personal care services related to: (a) the musculo-skeletal system; (b) the integumentary system; (c) the upper and lower gastrointestinal system; (d) the urinary system; (e) the cardiovascular and respiratory systems (vital signs, antiembolic stockings, oxygen assistance, positioning); (f) the neurological system (cognitive impairment, seizure disorder, post-stroke care, rehabilitation or restorative care); (g) the endocrine system (foot care, skin care and nutrition for a client with diabetes); (h) the promotion of sleep. If direct observation is impractical or intrusive, the Nurse Supervisor may ask the CHHA to describe how the task would be performed.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 1(a)-(h)

required_items.text: Written testing, oral testing or direct observation of the CHHA's knowledge and communication skills in: (a) observation, reporting and documentation of patient status and care furnished; (b) basic infection control procedures; (c) basic elements of body mechanics and functioning, and changes in body function that must be reported to the Nurse Supervisor; (d) maintenance of a clean, safe and healthy environment; (e) recognizing emergencies and knowledge of emergency procedures; (f) physical, emotional and developmental needs of and ways to work with the populations served, including respect for the patient and the patient's privacy and property; (g) adequate nutrition and fluid intake.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 2(a)-(g)

required_items.text: The clinical competency of every CHHA is tested or assessed throughout the year, through direct observation of skills with assigned patients and/or written or oral testing as in items 1 and 2 above.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Testing or assessment throughout the year

required_items.text: Competency documentation in the employee file includes: (1) name of the CHHA; (2) clinical skills tested, and the date and location of testing; (3) an evaluation of the CHHA's competency; (4) date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor performing the testing. At minimum, an assessment of competency is recorded by the end of each year of employment. Records may be electronic.

Policies and procedures relating to assignment of individuals, for the appropriate level of care, authorized to provide required service, assuring that Certified Nurse Assistants (CNAs) and unlicensed assistive personnel are not assigned to perform in-home personal care services.
The requirement for licensed and certified personnel to provide proof of New Jersey licensure or certification (out-of-state certifications are not valid for New Jersey in-home personal care).
Reporting of patient complaints to the agency
Agency's response to alleged reports of misconduct, violation of laws/regulations and unethical practices
Confidentiality requirements
Protection for those reporting unethical, fraudulent or illegal activity ("whistle-blower" protection)
Reporting of safety concerns and violations of law to licensing and/or regulatory agencies, as required by law
A procedure by which an RN, LPN, CHHA or other clinical staff can reach an RN for clinical questions at all times, in no less than one hour, with an RN on call during all hours of service.
Patients and family/significant others are provided with full and truthful disclosure of all information concerning fees and billing policies.

Every certified homemaker-home health aide or health care professional regulated by the Division wears an identification tag at all times while providing care. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, the term for the level of licensure or certification, and a photograph. Letters are of equal size, no smaller than one-quarter inch, and the tag is at least as large as any other identification worn.
Every health care service firm provides patient/employers with a copy of the Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides published by the NJ Board of Nursing.
The Consumer Guide is provided at least 24 hours before services are provided.
A patient/employer may waive the 24-hour timing in writing. The firm keeps the waiver for at least two years and still provides the information before services begin.
To place certified homemaker-home health aides, an agency regulated by the Division must be licensed as a health care service firm.
A health care service firm only refers or places actively certified homemaker-home health aides who are employed by the agency.
A homemaker-home health aide employed by an HCSF only performs tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor.
The health care practitioner supervisor ensures the aide demonstrates competence to perform the client care that is delegated.
The health care practitioner supervisor documents in the patient's record every task delegated to a homemaker-home health aide.

Prohibited acts: (1) recruiting, advertising or contracting for health care services without first obtaining registration; (2) charging a fee or liquidated damages to employees (this requires an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2); (3) preventing employees by contract from working for others (the same licensing consequence applies if a fee is charged); (4) knowingly sending staff to a facility where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers.

sections: I. Definitions (reference only; no policy items)

notes: No single official Division checklist or form lists the written policies for an HCSF. The binding rules (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3 and 13.5) cover only application paperwork, which was excluded. The Division's FAQ (HCSF-FAQ-07242025.pdf) also lists only application items: registration form, fee, formation documents, criminal-history certifications, $1M liability insurance, bond, practitioner-supervisor designation, and out-of-state licenses. The only official source that enumerates policy content is the Division's advisory 'Best Practices for Health Care Service Firms' (April 15, 2014). It says it is non-binding and that the statute and rules control, even where it uses 'shall'. Organize the manual in its order: II Clinical, III Personnel, IV Administrative, with the binding rule items (13:45B-13.6, 13.7, 14.7) cross-referenced in the matching policies. Registration is submitted online through the NJ Regulated Business Licensure Portal, and policies are not part of that submission. Keep the manual available for the Division's inspection and for the accrediting body, since HCSFs must obtain DHS-recognized accreditation within 12 months of registration. I did not fetch the NJ DHS-recognized accreditation standards or the Medicaid (PCA, MLTSS, PPP) manuals, so any added requirements from those sources are not captured here. Registration timing and financial reporting are in flux under P.L. 2026, c.45, and the Division says rule updates are pending. The 13:45B-13.3, 13:45B-14.7, 13:45B-13.6 and 13:45B-13.7 text came from Cornell LII mirrors, not the NJ Administrative Code directly. The Division's Subchapter 14 PDF could not be fetched. The Best Practices item IDs use my own section/heading plus the document's list number, because the document numbers each list separately and has no global item numbers.
